summary.prose: Building this Story means fixing a ledger record that quietly says nothing. Four defects compound: the change-set collector asks git only about the working tree, which is clean exactly when it runs; two fields are rendered but never written; the Trivial route uses a renderer that reads none of them; and a shared validate path overwrites a flag it cannot know, flipping records between renderers. The work is therefore less about new capability than about removing a dependence on luck — derive the change set from the Story's committed range, give the two dead fields producers, and collapse two renderers into one that shows whatever a record actually holds. The shape of the build is characterise-first: the three defects are committed as tests that assert the WRONG behaviour and are each inverted by a named later task, so every fix is proved by flipping a baseline rather than by assertion, and three goldens captured from real pre-fix artifacts guard the 63 BUILD records already written.

tasks.title: Characterise all three defects as failing baselines, as separate tests with declared inversion points
tasks.summary: Drive a standalone build through implement then validate against a throwaway git repo and capture the record AS IT IS TODAY, as EXPECTATIONS OF THE WRONG BEHAVIOUR, so every later task diffs against a baseline and the fix is proved by a red-to-green transition rather than asserted. s1 established the flip by reading code (c14); this makes it observable. The three defects invert at THREE DIFFERENT tasks, so they must be separately-named tests each naming its inversion point IN the test name: the lost '## Scope' inverts at t8 (the converged renderer emits Scope whenever body.focus is present, regardless of the flag), the forced meta.standalone false inverts at t9, and the empty change set inverts at t6. Treating them as one unit would make t8 look like a regression and invite the build to 'fix' it by reverting an improvement. MUST be first: written after any fix, it encodes the fixed behaviour and proves nothing.
acceptanceChecks: TEST A, named for its t8 inversion point: a standalone record driven through implement-then-validate renders md containing NO '## Scope' while the json still carries body.focus — the orphaned-content defect

TEST C, named for its t6 inversion point: on a CLEAN working tree collectBuildChangeLog returns [] and the persisted record has no '## Changes' section
All three PASS on unmodified HEAD (they characterise, they do not yet demand), and each carries a comment naming the exact task that will invert it
The throwaway-repo harness follows the committed gate idiom at diff-grounding.test.ts:150 and asserts read-only afterwards via rev-list --count and status --porcelain

citations.quotedText: Derived from the ISSUE fixIntent plus the constraint that correctness must not depend on an instruction being followed: the derivation uses the Story's committed range when the tree is clean and the working tree when it is not.

citations.ref: LLD S001 ac2 — the record's own artifact paths are excluded from the change set
citations.quotedText: The record must never claim the Story changed its own BUILD.md or BUILD json; the exclusion applies to both derivations, asserted separately.

citations.ref: LLD S001 ac3 — body.summary and body.commit have producers and omit cleanly
citations.quotedText: A supplied summary is persisted and rendered; an empty, whitespace-only or absent one omits the key. body.commit comes from HEAD and is omitted when HEAD cannot be read.

citations.ref: LLD S001 ac4 — provenance renders on EVERY route, not only the plan-driven one
citations.quotedText: A trivial-routed build's record must render the same provenance sections a plan-driven one does, which it structurally cannot do today because the standalone renderer reads none of those fields.

citations.ref: LLD S001 ac5 — the renderer flip is closed from both directions, with no churn on written artifacts
citations.quotedText: The standalone flag no longer selects a renderer and is no longer asserted by the shared validate path; a record carrying no new content renders byte-identically to today.

citations.ref: LLD S001 ac6 — nothing throws and no existing caller changes behaviour
citations.quotedText: collectBuildChangeLog never throws; existing two-argument call sites behave identically; an empty or absent changeLog renders no '## Changes' section.

citations.ref: LLD S001 §6 Migration — the nine ordered, independently-rollbackable steps
citations.quotedText: step1 characterise; step2 capture byte-identity baselines from REAL pre-fix records; step3 widen the derivation additively; step4 apply the exclusion to both derivations; step5 resolve and pass the range base with no HEAD^ fallback; step6 give commit and summary producers; step7 converge the renderers keeping a delegating shim; step8 stop validate asserting standalone:false; step9 re-run the suites and verify forward compatibility.

citations.ref: plan open-question resolution q0b544035 — recorded base with PLAN-commit fallback
citations.quotedText: The base is STAMPED at approval (meta.rangeBase); the PLAN-introducing commit is the fallback for already-written records; if NEITHER resolves, log and return empty — correcting the option's 'fail with an error' clause, which contradicts ac6. Grounded on the finding that approval and commit are SEPARATE events: bfe98ff7 s4's PLAN was approved at 05:50:05Z and first committed 15s later in 87f3f2f, and this Story's own LLD was approved-and-untracked at resolution time.

citations.ref: plan open-question resolution q0c5270ce — rename renderPlanBuildRecordMd in this Story
citations.quotedText: Rename to renderBuildRecordMd as an explicit plan task rather than slipping it into the build; no deprecated alias, since renderStandaloneBuildRecordMd is already retained as the compatibility shim. Sizing corrected from 'two call sites' to 1 production site plus ~17 test references that must be RUN, not merely compiled.

citations.ref: plan open-question resolution q378acc65 — a failed collection stays indistinguishable in the ARTIFACT, visible in the LOG
citations.quotedText: No tri-state field and no renderer change; the LLD's settled answer stands. But the failure path must remain clearly distinguishable in the log — the existing log call must survive the refactor and be ASSERTED, since under ac6's never-throw behaviour a swallowed exception is the only trace there is.

citations.ref: ISSUE-93081bff91ae5108 fixIntent — the tracked source of intent for this bugfix
citations.quotedText: A completed Story's BUILD ledger record must carry what the Story actually changed, a summary of the changes, and the commit it landed in — on every route. A bugfix routed through `issue` takes its intent from the ISSUE rather than from an Epic's Stories, so ac1-ac6 are DERIVED from this plus the two judging constraints.

citations.ref: ISSUE-93081bff91ae5108 judging constraint 1 — correctness must not depend on an instruction being followed
citations.quotedText: The collector is wrong because it depends on the implement prompt's commit-before-validate instruction actually being followed. Every fix must hold regardless of whether a prompt, a convention or a human step was honoured.

citations.ref: ISSUE-93081bff91ae5108 judging constraint 2 — no unnecessary churn on already-written artifacts
citations.quotedText: 63 BUILD records and 648 artifacts are already committed. A record carrying no new content must render byte-identically to today, proved against REAL pre-fix fixtures rather than constructed ones, which would agree with the fix by construction.
